findings: Old 6–67,89–93,377–381 and new 7–14,18–36,266–282,398–412 show US merchant/customer and USD, a 3/6/12/18-installment BNPL redirect, customer authorization and Sunbit collection, and an exact USD 60.00–19,999.99 range. November explicitly says single-use, domestic only, B2C not B2B, instant provisional access with possible review after activation, and standard payout. Customer logs in/creates account on Sunbit on desktop or mobile, selects plan, accepts terms, and authorizes. The November overview’s depicted customer experience (new 398–412) shows return and immediate success notification in its completed-payment step. Sunbit collects installments. That depiction is separate from versioned manual capture, where authorization precedes an explicit capture request within the authorization window (June 24 Dahlia changelog 7–23; new 281–295), and from standard payout (new 14). Sunbit/partner bank decides customer eligibility and has the sole right to payment; Stripe acquires and settles. 'Paid up front/instantly' is not immediate bank payout. Customer completes application/reviews terms, no surcharging, and financed amount including down payment cannot exceed delivered goods/rendered services price (old 313–320; new 27–36). Appeals for rejected/offboarded account or capability restrictions go to Stripe Support coordinating with Sunbit (new 23–36).

Old label list at 95–311 has 213 bullets including duplicates and an Other categories line, not approximately 175 as source 13/29. New 38–264 introduces code-keyed eligibility and general prohibited versus restricted terms; all 220 table rows are marked Prohibited. Specific coding and new listed rows such as 4829, 6399 and 9405 (new 71,181,261) improve retrieval and are substantive documentation changes, but changed presence does not establish newly prohibited or permitted categories. Account-type marketplace Connect support at new 20 does not erase prohibition of MCC 5262 (new 97) or the review requirement.

May raw 44–46 and source 13/17 mark manual capture unavailable. The captured 2026-06-24.dahlia changelog lines 1–23 explicitly adds manual capture for Sunbit PaymentIntents and documents Checkout and payment-method-specific paths. In that versioned manual flow, merchant authorization and capture are separate: an explicit capture request within the authorization window collects the funds (changelog 7–23). Its Checkout endpoint link has a distinct 2026-05-27.dahlia query. Preserve version qualification and unresolved source disagreement rather than inferring universal account support or selecting a winning source for setup_future_usage.

November product/API matrix new 371–395 explicitly supports full page, Payment Links, embedded form, Payment Element, in-app, Connect, Checkout Sessions and PaymentIntents. May listed Checkout, Elements, Payment Links and Connect, with setup/subscription mode and Express Checkout exclusions (old 58–67,74–87). The November route still offers Dashboard enablement with Stripe relevance selection or a linked manual-integration guide (new 422–426). Preserve old platform and selected connected accounts active sunbit_payments, five old charge routing descriptor mappings, and version them as May authority (old 355–375; source 27). New 414–420 adds customer statement merchant identifier, PaymentIntent descriptor/default and latest_charge.payment_method_details.sunbit.transaction_id, plus a Connect descriptor pointer. Omission of the old Connect section is not withdrawal.

Old 322–344 and new 322–365 preserve balance hold, 12 calendar days for merchant evidence, provider decision and balance result. It distinguishes full and partial dispute support (new 303–305) and adds Sunbit customer-fraud loss coverage with a promptly honored Stripe request to stop/pause shipment (new 367–369). Eligibility/offboarding appeals differ from nonappealable dispute outcomes. Preserve May listed fraud, duplicate payment and amount mismatch dispute reasons as dated.

Old 346–353 and new 297–320 describe full or partial 180-day asynchronous refunds, up to five minutes, success/failure status and event, and alternate method after failure restores Stripe balance. Source lines 23–25 preserve parts of the old summary but need November state/action boundaries.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw `raw/stripe-payments-sunbit-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-sunbit-2025.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-sunbit.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/sunbit`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: The November 7, 2026 capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/sunbit describes single-use domestic US B2C BNPL for USD 60.00 to 19,999.99. Eligible US merchant and Connect account types get provisional access subject to review and prohibited MCCs; the customer completes their application, accepts Sunbit terms and authorizes the chosen installment plan at Sunbit. Sunbit or its bank decides customer eligibility and collects repayment, while Stripe acquires the purchase and uses its standard payout schedule (new raw lines 7-42 and 266-295). The November overview's depicted completed customer flow reports immediate success notification after authorization and return (new raw lines 398-412). November says manual capture is supported with no partial, multi- or over-capture, and the method matrix excludes setup_future_usage, SetupIntents and off-session payments. The November cross-BNPL matrix conflicts on capture and setup_future_usage, while the June 24 Dahlia changelog lines 7-23 document a versioned manual workflow. Authorization comes first and an explicit capture request within the authorization window collects funds. An authorized but uncaptured manual payment is still awaiting capture (new raw lines 281-295). May's overview and source-stripe-sunbit.md say no manual capture (old raw lines 44-67 and 89-97, new raw lines 281-305 and 371-395). Preserve the USD ceiling exactly, no surcharge and financing cap, 12 calendar days to contest, 180-day asynchronous refunds and May active Connect capability and descriptors. November adds the 35-day dispute decision and finality, refund cancellation/reversal restrictions, and transaction identifier retrieval (old raw lines 313-375, new raw lines 297-369 and 414-420). Commercial approval, capture and external payout remain distinct from customer return and from reading the documentation.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/sunbit, substantive documentation changes from May 6 to November 7, 2026 include provisional eligibility and account appeals, domestic B2C/marketplace account qualifications, prohibited MCC coding, manual capture support with exclusions, more explicit product/API coverage, refund constraints, dispute timing/finality/fraud handling and transaction identifiers (old raw lines 44-97 and 313-375, new raw lines 18-45, 266-369 and 371-420). Exact USD 60.00 to 19,999.99, US/ USD, no recurring, installment choice, surcharge and financing conditions, and dated May Connect capability and five charge-type descriptor mappings should survive. Preserve the dated May no-manual-capture label, the November method and comparison matrix conflicts on manual capture and setup_future_usage, and the 2026-06-24.dahlia changelog support within the authorization window. An eligible Connect account type does not waive prohibited MCC 5262, and the immediate payment wording does not change standard payout. The reordering, formatting and navigation links are presentation. The omission of the old demo and detailed Connect configuration does not prove capability withdrawal. Update source-stripe-sunbit.md while preserving its May raw, the root-to-Stripe index route, the reciprocal Stripe BNPL concept/source route, and distinct acceptance, overview and changelog evidence.

concept_targets.scope: Audit relevant sections first; only bounded evidence-backed reciprocal corrections in final reviewed findings. No unrelated rewrite.
